question: Should OpenClaw expose a configurable host filesystem path policy in core, and what canonical `tools.fs` contract plus exec scope should be supported?
rationale: This adds a public config surface and a security enforcement boundary, while live related PRs show competing API shapes and unresolved exec coverage.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
options.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization and symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing an implementation.

options.title: Land file-tool policy and split exec
options.body: Accept a file-tool-only first version only if shell-mediated access is clearly documented and a separate exec policy issue remains linked.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACL config if maintainers want core to rely on OS permissions, sandbox backends, and `workspaceOnly` only.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical allow/deny or roots model with deny precedence, normalization and symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and upgrade tests before landing an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged-history and prior-review signal on the existing workspace-only filesystem boundary.
